title: The DDL of proceeds beyond its columns is not published: constraint names, index names, index columns and the Field IDs of the 7 standard columns
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2.md T3.0, T3.1, T3.3; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 001 Recovery tables for the 14 data products v1.md section 13
description: TSD P8 T3.1 gives the 9 business columns of proceeds with their data types and lengths, T3.0 gives the 7 standard columns as a list and no Field ID, and no source in the read set gives the primary-key name, the index names, the index column order beyond a leading column, or the Field IDs the one dictionary uses for is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at and updated_by; the legacy story names columns and Field IDs but not index or constraint names.
evidence: TSD P8 T3.0 lists the 7 standard columns with no Field ID; T3.1 gives DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 only; the legacy section 13 fixes the columns of data_product and the seed counts, and names no index
proposed: Name the key, the two indexes and the standard-column Field IDs at merge under the platform naming convention, and let the one dictionary's seed carry the standard-column Field IDs

title: TSD P8 T3.1 carries payment_match_rule as a second table of the module, and the Ownership Map gives P8 one table only
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2.md T3.1 (DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273); _work/msr/context/P8.md (Ownership rows owned by P8: Tables (1) proceeds); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P8 rwb-payment (Payment)/RWB P8 E2027 APP Payment matching rules with the data team v1.md (D-RCV-36 T10)
section: APP s1, s4, s8 (BR10), s11, s19
description: The technical specification of the module defines a second table of P8, payment_match_rule, with 13 fields for the match rule by version, while the Ownership Map gives P8 exactly one table and the matching-rule story records D-RCV-36 T10 as retiring payment_match_rule; the estate's own count of 92 tables and the split therefore need one ruling on whether any rule table of P8 exists in a schema.
evidence: TSD P8 T3.1 payment_match_rule (NEW) DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273; _work/msr/context/P8.md Tables (1) proceeds; RWB P8 E2027 APP s11: payment_match_rule is retired and is neither created nor read (D-RCV-36 T10)
proposed: Keep the ruling of D-RCV-36 T10: the match rules are rows of a rule package of rwb-decision and no payment_match_rule table is created in rwb_payment

title: The read paths that proceeds has to serve, and the screens that read it, are stated in no source of the read set
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2.md T-A.1, T-A.2; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3.md Screens
description: The two operations of the service give the query of GET /proceeds as matched, from, to, page and size and nothing else, and the FSD names SCR-28 and SCR-29 with a first-in epic and no field list, panel or state set; the index columns, the leading column of each read path and the field list of the two screens are therefore settled at design time and not taken from a source.
evidence: TSD P8 T-A.2 API-P8-001 request: Query matched, from, to, page, size; FSD P8 Screens: SCR-28 Proceeds matching, SCR-29 Posting, with no field list
proposed: Index the unmatched list on matched_to and received_date and the case read on case_id and received_date, and leave the screen field lists with the screen stories

title: The handover of a service's field declaration to the one dictionary has no documented mechanism or operation
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P1 rwb-source-data (Source data)/RWB P1 E1001 APP Recovery tables for the 14 data products v1.md section 1; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2.md T3.1; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01
description: The dictionary of 122 objects and 1,366 fields is held in rwb_source_data by RWB-P1-E1001-APP, and this service may neither write it nor read it at run time, while its own migration must prove its 9 field rows matched; no source names the operation, the file format or the register in which one service hands its field rows to that one seed.
evidence: RWB P1 E1001 APP holds the catalog and the dictionary in rwb_source_data; TSD P8 T3.1 gives the fields and no handover; DP-01 forbids the cross-schema write
proposed: Carry the declaration as a build artefact of this story, hand it to the one seed through the Change Register, and prove it matched by the conformance test

title: TSD P8 T3.3 declares three many-to-one relationships of proceeds and the target keeps them as values
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2.md T3.3; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 001 Recovery tables for the 14 data products v1.md AC1 and BR8
description: The technical specification relates proceeds to recovery_case, treatment and account_payment as many-to-one, and in the target the three owners sit in rwb_case, rwb_treatment and the ACE payment fact; account_payment has left the estate altogether, and the legacy rule holds that a link to another owner is a business key with no foreign key, so three declared relationships become three values and no constraint.
evidence: TSD P8 T3.3 relationships: proceeds to recovery_case, treatment, account_payment; legacy AC1: account_payment is one of the 20 tables that left the schema, and every link to an ACE record is a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key; legacy BR8
proposed: Keep case_id, treatment_id and account_payment_id as uuid values with no foreign key, and let the references be resolved through the owners' contracts

title: DP13 Money and closure is catalogued with the system of record ACE only, while the match on the same row is a Workbench record
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 001 Recovery tables for the 14 data products v1.md section 13 (DP13) and BR3; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P1 rwb-source-data (Source data)/RWB P1 E1001 APP Recovery tables for the 14 data products v1.md section 11 (DP13)
description: The catalog row of DP13 names the system of record ACE (ingested from ALS and GL) with refresh cycle DAILY and expected by 08:00, and the product holds two kinds of fact: the money the ACE batch reports and the match this service decides; legacy BR3 allows one sentence naming both where a product holds both, and the row names ACE only, so the single-row catalog answer and the Workbench match on the same row disagree.
evidence: Legacy section 13 DP13: ACE (ingested from ALS and GL); legacy BR3: one system of record written ACE (ingested from X), Recovery Workbench, or one sentence naming both where the product holds both
proposed: Keep DP13 as one product with one row, the money facts ACE's and the match the Workbench's, and correct the catalog wording in RWB-P1-E1001-APP under a new catalog version

title: The plan gives this story no H row, while its migration needs the schema, the login and the Flyway pipeline of the service
source: WP B2-P8-008 story JSON (H [], C [], I [], X []); Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.7; _work/msr/context/P8.md
description: A migration cannot run before the schema, its login and the per-service Flyway sequence exist, and the plan carries no H row for this story because those come with the service baseline that the platform contracts of the service supply; the six platform CON stories are therefore consumed as the baseline and are named in the preconditions rather than in the metadata row.
evidence: WP B2-P8-008 story JSON: H [], ready Day 1; Template and Rules R5.7 rules 1 and 5; the platform contracts RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-NF06-DB, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON
proposed: Keep the metadata row at None and Day 1, and carry the six platform contracts as the service baseline in the preconditions and the fakes

title: EP01's wave map wave is 1 and rwb-payment's Architecture v5 wave is 2 for the same story
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 and R6; _work/msr/context/P8.md (Wave 2); WP B2-P8-008 story JSON (wave 1, business_epic EP01)
description: The wave map places EP01 in wave 1 and Architecture v5 places rwb-payment in wave 2, so the story sits one wave before its service; the rule keeps the earlier wave and raises one conflict per service and business epic, which for P8 and EP01 is this story.
evidence: Template and Rules R5.6: a story whose W-MAP wave is earlier than its service's Arch v5 wave keeps the W-MAP wave, and one conflict gap is raised per service and business epic; P8 context pack Wave 2
proposed: Keep wave 1 and the release date 30 November 2026 unchanged and tentative, and review the service's wave at the verification loop
